deep.reconstruction:
Context (from p.225): we want two Pythagorean (rational right) triangles A and B, built from generators (p,q) and (r,s), whose areas are in a given ratio a:b. Up to a common factor the areas are A = pq(p^2-q^2) and B = rs(r^2-s^2). On p.225 Euler imposes ten linear relations between (r,s) and (p,q). Each one makes the area ratio a linear-fractional function of p/q. Solving it gives the ten parametric solutions I-X in terms of a and b. For example, VIII: r=p-q, s=2q gives A/B = p/(2p-6q) = a/b, so p:q = 6a:(2a-b).

This page: Euler keeps four of the ten, I, V, II and III, and pairs each with a 'socia' (companion). The companion comes from replacing the generators (p,q) by (p+q, p-q) and (r,s) by (r+s, r-s). The arabic numbers 1, 5, 2, 3 in the right-hand column of the lower block record which original solution each companion comes from. Explicitly:

- alpha, from I (p=a+b, q=2a-b, r=a+b, s=2b-a): (3a, 2b-a, 3b, 2a-b).
- beta, from V (2a+b, b-a, a+2b, b-a): (a+2b, 3a, 3b, b+2a).
- gamma, from II (b-2a, 6a, 2b-4a, b+4a): (b+4a, b-8a, 3b, 8a-b). Here r-s = b-8a is written with the opposite sign.
- delta, from III (b+2a, 6a, 2b+4a, b-4a): (b+8a, b-4a, 3b, 8a+b).

Why the companions work (my addition): the triangle with generators (p+q, p-q) has legs 4pq and 2(p^2-q^2). It is therefore the original triangle with its legs swapped and doubled, and its area is 4pq(p^2-q^2), i.e. 4A. Replacing both triangles this way multiplies A and B by 4, so the ratio a:b is preserved.

Signs: Euler's rule (p.225) is that negative generators may be replaced by their absolute values, with the larger value put in p (or r). The area magnitude |pq(p^2-q^2)| does not change under a sign flip, so writing 8a-b instead of b-8a is harmless.

Example 1 (a=2, b=1): every pair checks, with area ratio 2.
- alpha: (3,3,3,0) and (6,0,3,3). Both are degenerate (an area is 0).
- beta: (5,1,4,1) and (6,4,5,3). Areas 120:60 and 480:240.
- gamma: (12,3,9,6) and (15,9,15,3). Areas 4860:2430 and 19440:9720.
- delta: (12,5,10,7) and (17,7,17,3). Areas 7140:3570 and 28560:14280.

Example 2 (a=3, b=2), ratio 3/2:
- alpha: (5,4,5,1) and (9,1,6,4).
- beta: (8,1,7,1) and (9,7,8,6).
- gamma: (18,4,14,8), reduced by 2 to (9,2,7,4); the companion is (22,14,22,6), shown already reduced as (11,7,11,3).
- delta: (18,8,16,10), reduced to (9,4,8,5); the companion (26,10,26,6) is shown reduced as (13,5,13,3).

Example 3 (a=1, b=1):
- alpha: (2,1,2,1) and (3,1,3,1).
- beta: (3,0,3,0) and (3,3,3,3), degenerate.
- gamma: (6,1,5,2) and (7,5,7,3).
- delta: (6,3,6,3) and (9,3,9,3). Here A = B trivially.

The next page goes on to choose a and b as squares, so that AB is a square.
errors: No computational errors: every parametric companion and every numerical entry in the three examples checks.

Not an error but worth noting: each 'socia' gives the same pair of triangles up to similarity. The (p+q, p-q) triangle is the (p,q) triangle doubled with legs swapped. So the 'eight solutions' are really at most four distinct pairs of shapes. Euler does not say this here, although p.225 mentions excluding similar triangles.

Several listed solutions are degenerate and Euler gives them without comment: alpha in Ex.1 (s=0, q=0), beta in Ex.3 (q=0, p=q). Other cases are trivial (A identical to B), e.g. alpha, gamma-companion and delta in Ex.3, and the alpha first entry in Ex.1 being degenerate.
Sign slip, harmless under Euler's absolute-value rule: in gamma he writes s = 8a-b where the substitution gives r-s = b-8a.

results.what: Two Pythagorean triangles with areas in a prescribed ratio a:b: four linear-parametric families (I, V, II, III) in a and b, plus companions from (p,q) -> (p+q, p-q)
results.modern_name: Rational right triangles with areas in given ratio (congruent-number-type Diophantine problem); the generator map (p,q) -> (p+q, p-q) giving a similar triangle scaled by 2
results.usually_credited_to: Diophantine tradition (Diophantus, Fermat, Frenicle); the (p+q, p-q) similarity is classical folklore

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine parametric Diophantine work on Pythagorean triangles with a given area ratio, in Euler's well-known style. The companion trick only rescales the triangles. The editors note it was 'already worked out' (jam redacta).

checkable.sympy: a,b=symbols('a b'); T=lambda p,q: p*q*(p**2-q**2); simplify(T(a+b,2*a-b)*b - a*T(a+b,2*b-a))
checkable.asserts: Solution I gives area ratio a/b (expected 0).
Companion alpha gives area ratio a/b (expected 0).
Companion beta gives area ratio a/b.
Companion gamma (with s=b-8a) gives ratio a/b; with s=8a-b only the sign of B flips.
Companion delta: A = -(a/b)*B with the signs as printed, i.e. |A|/|B| = a/b.
The companion triangle's area is 4 times the original (expected 0).

transcription_corrections: The arabic column 1, 5, 2, 3 beside the companion rows alpha-delta refers to the source solutions I, V, II, III; the transcription is otherwise accurate against the image.
In Example 2, the braces join the row (18,4,14,8) with its halved form (9,2,7,4), and likewise (18,8,16,10) with (9,4,8,5); they show reduction by the common factor.
